transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lynn Harper (Havenbrook CISO), Evan Zhou (Head of Cloud Ops), Marisol Vega (Compliance), Aaron Patel (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick security review focused on data handling: audit logs, RBAC/SSO, KMS options, and explicit confirmation around training on customer data and prompt retention. Customer asked for artifact handoffs and a deeper runbook session.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture
- SSO (SAML / OIDC) and SCIM provisioning, RBAC model
- Audit logs: retention, export, and integrity guarantees
- Encryption: at-rest, in-transit, and customer-managed keys (BYOK) / HSM options
- Data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI flow, 'no-train' assurances and what that means operationally

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. I'm Samir from Redwood, with Priya our SE. We're here to walk through the security artifacts and answer detailed questions on data handling.
00:12 Lynn: Thanks, Samir. We want to make sure we cover two big things today — first the formal artifacts (SOC2/ISO) and then specific operational guarantees around prompt retention and training.
00:20 Priya: Great. I'll jump in on the technical bits. Quick housekeeping, Priya here — I'll share a diagram of the private deployment options and the KMS flows after the call.
00:32 Evan: For us, the gating items are: can we have customer-managed keys, what does the audit log look like (format, retention), and can you confirm we can get an on-prem/private deployment so data never leaves our VPC?
00:44 Priya: Yes on the private deployment. Redwood Private supports a VPC-only control plane option and an on-prem package for fully air-gapped needs. For hosted customers, we have regional tenancy and data residency controls in EU/US/APAC.
00:55 Lynn: On 'no training' — we've seen some vendors claim it but then have ambiguous language in EULAs. Is there a written, contractual no-training guarantee?
01:05 Samir: Short answer: yes. By default Redwood does not train models on customer prompts or responses. We maintain a no-train policy for hosted and private deployments unless there's an explicit opt-in (we call it data opt-in for model improvement). We'll provide the exact clause for your legal team.
01:20 Marisol: And is that enforceable technically? Like, where is the data pathway prevented from being piped to training buckets?
01:27 Priya: Operationally we separate ingestion pipelines. Customer request logs and telemetry are stored in segregated buckets with access controls audited by SOC2 controls. Training data pipelines are entirely separate systems with their own access controls and have no read permissions to those buckets. There is additional isolation for Dedicated and Private where we don't even route to central telemetry.
01:46 Evan: Ok. For KMS — we want BYOK and key rotation under our control. Does Redwood support external key wraps / importable keys or HSM integration?
01:55 Priya: We support AWS KMS CMKs for hosted customers, and for Private/Dedicated we offer HSM or RHSM integrations. BYOK with key wrapping and import is supported; we can also do integration with an HSM-backed KMS and customer-managed key stores. We'll attach a diagram and steps.
02:12 Lynn: Audit logs — what fields are included and how long are they retained by default? Also immutability?
02:20 Priya: Default audit retention for hosted is 90 days; for enterprise plans we offer 1 year by default and longer with the audit-retention add-on (up to 7 years). Logs are tamper-evident: we sign batches and maintain append-only stores, and we can export logs via S3 with an event hashing scheme; we also provide a signed manifest on request.
02:36 Evan: Do you support streaming logs to our Splunk or SIEM?
02:40 Priya: Yes, we have native integrations and log-forwarding agents — Splunk, Datadog, Sumo are supported; we can set up a secure push or your syslog endpoint.
02:48 Lynn: Can the audit exports be scoped per-customer and per-model? We need per-model traceability for PII resurfacing investigations.
02:55 Priya: Yes, audit records include request metadata, model id, route, token usage, and a hash of the prompt (we also have optional prompt redaction). You can configure whether prompt content is included in the logs or only a hashed reference.
03:10 Aaron: From procurement — pricing aside — we need to see the SOC2 Type II report and ISO cert and a summary of the last pen test.
03:18 Samir: We'll provide the SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate, and a redacted penetration test summary. We'll redact customer-identifying info.
03:25 Marisol: About PII/PHI — does Redwood perform any content scanning that might store sensitive content? Like DLP or PII scrubbing that touches the data?
03:33 Priya: We have optional content classifiers that can run for quality/monitoring but they're opt-in. For customers that require zero content processing, you'll choose no content-classifiers and we won't persist prompts beyond the configured retention window.
03:46 Evan: How does prompt retention work in hosted mode vs private?
03:50 Priya: Hosted default: ephemeral caching for K V (KV) cache to speed up repeated requests, retention for analytic logs is 90 days unless you buy extended retention. Prompts can be set to be ephemeral — deleted immediately after response — or retained for x-days per customer policy. Private deployments give you complete control — you can set retention to zero and disable analytics.
04:07 Lynn: For legal, we need explicit language that prompt content will not be used to improve Redwood models and will not be retained beyond agreed retention unless we opt in. Will you include that in the contract?
04:18 Samir: Absolutely. We'll include contract language and a short addendum that defines retention windows and the no-training guarantee. We'll also add the technical enforcement description Priya mentioned.
04:25 Evan: SSO and identity. We use SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We want RBAC that maps to our AD groups.
04:32 Priya: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC SSO, and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. RBAC is role-based plus group mapping — you can map AD groups to Redwood roles and create custom roles for narrow admin privileges. We log all admin actions in the audit trail.
04:50 Lynn: Is there a separate 'super-admin' account or break-glass procedure?
04:54 Priya: There's a configurable break-glass flow. You can require MFA for escalation and we emit special escalation events to the audit log with approver metadata.
05:02 Aaron: On data residency, if we want all logs and models in a single region (us-east-1) is that possible?
05:07 Priya: Yes, we can pin tenancy to us-east-1 for both compute and storage with Private or Dedicated deployments. Hosted customers can select region tenancy depending on plan and capacity.
05:16 Lynn: One more — encryption in transit, TLS ciphers, and FIPS compliance?
05:20 Priya: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, TLS termination can be customer-controlled in Private setups. FIPS-compliant HSMs are supported for key storage if you need FIPS modules.
05:28 Marisol: Do you provide metrics for access review? We have quarterly access reviews that require an exported list of active users and granted roles.
05:34 Priya: Yes, we provide an access report CSV via the console and can automate monthly exports to your S3.
05:40 Lynn: For eDiscovery and legal holds — if there's a subpoena, what's the process?
05:44 Samir: We have a legal intake process; we'll surface the steps and contact. For Private deployments you're the controller with primary custody; for hosted we'll work with legal after validating the subpoena. We can provide time-to-respond SLAs in enterprise contracts.
05:55 Evan: Ok that mostly covers our questions. Can you also confirm how you prevent prompts from being used as training signal in internal eval systems?
06:02 Priya: Internal evals use synthetic data or internal prompts only. Customer data is tagged and excluded from any model improvement flows by policy and access controls; audits check show no access.
06:12 Lynn: Great. We'll need the explicit clause and the SOC2 artifacts. Also please add the runbook session for network testing.
06:18 Samir: Noted. We'll send the artifacts and schedule the runbook demo with Evan.

Recap & next steps (verbal):
- Redwood to share SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, redacted pentest summary, and contract addendum with no-train language.
- Priya to share KMS/BYOK diagrams, SCIM/SAML config examples, and audit log export format.
- Schedule technical runbook with Evan and Priya to test VPC allowlist and log forwarding.

End of transcript.
